# Phase 0 Research: Application Foundation & Catalog Vertical Slice

**Feature**: `002-catalog-foundation` | **Date**: 2026-07-28 | **Plan**: [plan.md](./plan.md)

All Technical Context unknowns are resolved below. Findings marked **[verified]** were confirmed by executing the command/query on this machine during Phase 0; the rest are design decisions.

---

## 1. Platform version: .NET 10 + ABP 10.5.0

**Decision**: Target **.NET 10 (`net10.0`)** with **ABP 10.5.0**, generated by the **legacy `Volo.Abp.Cli` 10.5.0** installed as a **repo-local** dotnet tool:

```bash
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install Volo.Abp.Cli --version 10.5.0
dotnet abp new ToolShare -t app -u blazor-webapp -d ef --dbms postgresql -v 10.5.0 -csf false -o .
```

> ✅ **This decision matches constitution v2.0.0 Principle I.** Constitution v1.0.0 originally mandated .NET 9; the amendment to v2.0.0 (ratified 2026-07-28) retargeted Principle I to .NET 10 / ABP 10.5.x — see [plan.md](./plan.md#constitution-amendment-history-principle-i) and the constitution's Sync Impact Report.

**Rationale**:
- **[verified]** ABP `10.5.0` is published and complete on NuGet across every package this feature needs (`Volo.Abp.Core`, `Volo.Abp.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSql`, `Volo.Abp.BlobStoring.FileSystem`, `Volo.Abp.Cli`). `10.6.0` also exists; **10.5.0 is used because it was explicitly requested**, and pinning an exact version beats tracking the tip.
- **[verified]** A probe generation with `-v 10.5.0` produced a solution whose every `src/*.csproj` and `test/*.csproj` declares `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>`, with ABP `PackageReference`s at `10.5.0`, EF Core tooling at `10.0.7`, and **`Build succeeded`**.
- **[verified]** The project layout is **identical** to the 9.3.7 template — same ten `src/` projects, same five `test/` projects. The retarget is therefore a version change, not a restructuring: sections 2, 4, 6–12 of this document are unaffected.
- **[verified]** The machine has SDK `10.0.301` and runtime `10.0.9`, so no SDK install is required. Commit a `global.json` pinning `10.0.301` with `rollForward: latestFeature` so builds are identical for every developer and inside Docker.
- Pinning with `-v` still matters: **[verified]** the globally installed **ABP Studio CLI 3.0.7/3.0.8** exposes no template-version flag (only `--trust-version`), so it would silently generate whatever is current (10.6.0 today, something else tomorrow). The legacy CLI's `-v` gives a reproducible generation.
- Installing it **repo-locally** (`dotnet abp …`) avoids clobbering the user's global ABP Studio CLI, and the committed `dotnet-tools.json` makes generation reproducible on any machine — Principle VI.

**Alternatives considered**:
- *Stay on .NET 9 / ABP 9.3.7*: was compliant with constitution v1.0.0, and **[verified]** working — but it contradicted an explicit instruction, and .NET 9 is the trailing release. Migrating a delivered modular monolith later costs a coordinated port across every module; migrating now costs a version bump. This tradeoff is why Principle I was amended to v2.0.0 rather than the plan staying on .NET 9.
- *ABP 10.6.0 (the current tip)*: newer, but 10.5 was specified. Revisit at the next planned upgrade.
- *ABP Studio CLI without a version pin*: convenient, but non-reproducible — the generated version drifts with the tool.
- *Hand-build from `dotnet new classlib` + ABP NuGet packages*: full control, but re-implements OpenIddict/Identity/Blazor host wiring the template already gets right; weeks of avoidable work.

## 1a. EF Core tooling prerequisite (new in .NET 10)

**Decision**: Require **`dotnet-ef` 10.x**; add `dotnet tool update -g dotnet-ef --version 10.*` to the prerequisites, and prefer the **repo-local** manifest entry so the version travels with the repo.

**Rationale**: **[verified]** this is not theoretical — the ABP 10.5 probe generation **built successfully but failed at the initial-migration step**:

```
The Entity Framework tools version '9.0.9' is older than that of the runtime '10.0.7'.
System.MissingMethodException: Method not found:
  'System.String Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Diagnostics.AbstractionsStrings.ArgumentIsEmpty(System.Object)'
```

**[verified]** the machine's global tool is `dotnet-ef 9.0.9`. EF Core design-time tooling is not forward-compatible: a 9.x tool cannot scaffold a 10.x model. Every `dotnet ef migrations add` in this plan — including the Catalog module's initial migration — fails until the tool is upgraded. This was invisible on .NET 9 and is the single concrete piece of developer-environment fallout from the platform bump.

**Alternatives considered**: *pin `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tools` per project only* (the package reference is already at 10.0.7 in the template; the failure comes from the **global tool**, so it does not help); *generate migrations inside a container* (works, but makes the ordinary inner loop depend on Docker for no benefit).

---

## 2. Modular-monolith shape: module projects vs. the `-t module` template

**Decision**: Add Catalog as **six sibling projects under `src/`** in the host solution (`ToolShare.Catalog.Domain.Shared`, `.Domain`, `.Application.Contracts`, `.Application`, `.EntityFrameworkCore`, `.Blazor`), each with its own `AbpModule` class, wired into the host by `[DependsOn]`. Do **not** use `abp new … -t module`.

**Rationale**: **[verified]** the `-t module` template generates a *standalone module solution* with its own host application, its own test host and its own DbMigrator — infrastructure the monolith already owns, and which would have to be deleted or kept dead. The six-project shape is exactly what Principle II prescribes, and repeating it per module (`ToolShare.Membership.*`, `ToolShare.Lending.*`) keeps the file tree self-documenting.

**Alternatives considered**:
- *`-t module` then prune*: more deletion work than creation work, and leaves the module's NuGet-packaging plumbing behind.
- *Folder-per-module inside a single set of layer projects*: cheapest to create, but boundaries become a naming convention a compiler cannot enforce — precisely the "big ball of mud wearing the costume of structure" Principle II names.

---

## 3. Blazor render mode

**Decision**: Generate with `-u blazor-webapp` (Blazor Web App), then force **InteractiveServer globally** and delete the WebAssembly half: remove `src/ToolShare.Blazor.Client`, `src/ToolShare.HttpApi.Client`, `test/ToolShare.HttpApi.Client.ConsoleTestApp`; in `ToolShareBlazorModule` drop `AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents()` / `AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode()` and set the LeptonX `Parameters.InteractiveAuto = false`.

**Rationale**: Principle I says "Blazor Web App in **InteractiveServer** mode". **[verified on ABP 10.5]** the template still ships `AddInteractiveServerComponents()` **and** `AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents()` with `InteractiveAuto = true` — i.e. Auto render mode, which is neither what the constitution says nor what the feature needs. Server-only rendering also lets Catalog UI components call application services **in-process**, so no HTTP proxy layer or client DTO duplication is needed for the slice. `ToolShare.HttpApi` is kept because the ABP Account/Identity endpoints the host uses live there.

**Alternatives considered**:
- *`-u blazor-server` (classic Blazor Server)*: simpler, but it is the legacy hosting model, not the "Blazor Web App" the constitution names.
- *Keep `Blazor.Client` and merely set the render mode*: leaves an unused WASM project, its build cost and its bundling step in every CI run.

## 4. Database topology, schema isolation and migrations

**Decision**: One PostgreSQL 16 database `toolshare`. Host `ToolShareDbContext` → schema `public`. `CatalogDbContext : AbpDbContext<CatalogDbContext>` → `modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema("catalog")`, registered with `UseNpgsql(o => o.MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", "catalog"))`. Each module's `*.EntityFrameworkCore` project declares its **own** migrator interface (`ICatalogDbSchemaMigrator`) and implementation; `ToolShare.DbMigrator`, as composition root, references both EF projects and runs them in order.

**Rationale**: Principle III requires per-module DbContext + schema and forbids cross-schema FKs. A separate migrations-history table per schema lets each module's migrations evolve independently. Letting each module own its migrator interface avoids the alternative trap — Catalog's EF project referencing the *host's* `ToolShare.Domain` for a shared `IToolShareDbSchemaMigrator`, which would be a module→host-Domain reference of exactly the kind Principle II forbids. Only `DbMigrator` (and the host) know about all modules, which is what a composition root is for.

**Cross-schema references**: `Tool.CategoryId`, `ToolInstance.ToolId`, `Photo.ToolInstanceId`, `StateChange.ToolInstanceId` are all *within* `catalog` and keep real FKs. Identity references (`CreatorId`, `LastModifierId`, `ChangedByUserId`) are plain `uuid` columns with **no** FK to `public."AbpUsers"` — ABP's audit properties already behave this way, so nothing must be un-done.

**Alternatives considered**: *database-per-module* (over-engineering for a monolith serving one community, and it breaks the single-`docker compose` promise); *shared schema with table prefixes* (violates Principle III outright).

---

## 5. Integration-test isolation with real PostgreSQL

**Decision**: `Testcontainers.PostgreSql` **4.13.0** running `postgres:16-alpine`. One container per test assembly (xUnit collection fixture in `ToolShare.TestBase`). At fixture start, create a **template database**, apply all EF migrations to it once, then give each test class a fresh database via `CREATE DATABASE test_<guid> TEMPLATE toolshare_template`. Remove `Volo.Abp.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite` and the generated `ConfigureInMemorySqlite` wiring from the host test module.

**Rationale**: Principle V forbids in-memory/SQLite substitutes *because schema mapping and provider behavior are under test* — and this slice depends on exactly that: a case-insensitive unique index on `NormalizedSerialNumber`, `catalog`-schema mapping, and Npgsql concurrency-token behavior. **[verified on ABP 10.5]** the generated `ToolShare.EntityFrameworkCore.Tests` still references `Volo.Abp.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite 10.5.0` and wires `ConfigureInMemorySqlite`, so this is a removal the plan must schedule, not an addition.

**.NET 10 impact**: none on the test stack. **[verified]** ABP 10.5 still generates **xUnit 2.9.3** (with `xunit.runner.visualstudio` 3.1.4 and `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` 17.14.1) — **no xUnit v3 migration is in scope**, so ABP's `AbpIntegratedTest` base and the collection-fixture pattern below are unchanged. `Testcontainers.PostgreSql` 4.13.0 targets netstandard2.0 and runs on `net10.0` unchanged. PostgreSQL's `CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE` is a file-level copy: per-class isolation costs milliseconds rather than a container start or a full migration run.

**Alternatives considered**:
- *Truncate all `catalog` tables between tests*: viable fallback, but leaks sequence state and requires maintaining a truncate list as the schema grows. Keep as plan B if template-copy proves awkward on any platform.
- *Transaction-per-test with rollback*: cleanest in theory, but ABP's unit-of-work commits inside the code under test, so the boundary is not ours to control.
- *One container per test class*: correct but roughly an order of magnitude slower to start.

## 6. Accent- and case-tolerant search (SC-008)

**Decision**: Persist a computed `NormalizedName` on `Tool` (and `Category`), produced by a **pure domain function** `CatalogTextNormalizer.Normalize(string)`: trim → collapse inner whitespace → `Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormD)` → drop `NonSpacingMark` characters → upper-case with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` → `Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormC)`. Search matches `NormalizedName LIKE '%' || @normalizedTerm || '%'` over a B-tree-indexed column. Serial numbers use the same normalizer for `NormalizedSerialNumber`, which carries the catalog-wide **unique** index.

**Rationale**: Meets both halves of SC-008 with no database extension, so the same behavior holds on the Testcontainers image and any managed PostgreSQL. It keeps the rule in the Domain layer where the Technology & Architecture Constraints section says pure algorithms belong, making it unit-testable without a database. For Ukrainian input the decomposition step folds `й→И` and `ї→І`, which is the desired tolerance for typo-prone data entry.

**Alternatives considered**: *`unaccent` + `citext` extensions* (needs `CREATE EXTENSION` with elevated privileges at migration time and pushes the rule into SQL, out of unit-test reach); *`ILIKE` only* (case-insensitive but not accent-tolerant — fails SC-008); *full-text search / `pg_trgm`* (substantial machinery for a catalog of a few thousand rows).

---

## 7. Photo storage

**Decision**: **ABP BlobStoring with the FileSystem provider** (`Volo.Abp.BlobStoring.FileSystem`, free). A typed container `ToolInstancePhotoContainer` maps to `/app/blobs/tool-instance-photos`, backed by a named Docker volume. The database stores only photo metadata (`FileName`, `ContentType`, `SizeBytes`, `BlobName`, `DisplayOrder`, `IsPrimary`). Limits come from `CatalogPhotoOptions` bound to the `Catalog:Photos` configuration section: `MaxSizeBytes` = 5 MB, `AllowedContentTypes` = `image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp`, `MaxPerInstance` = 5 — matching the spec's stated assumptions while remaining configurable.

**Rationale**: BlobStoring is the ABP-native abstraction, so swapping to S3/Azure later is a provider change with no domain impact. Keeping binaries out of PostgreSQL keeps backups and query plans sane. `IOptions`-bound configuration is simpler than an ABP `SettingDefinitionProvider` and sufficient — nothing in the spec requires runtime, per-user or per-tenant tuning of these limits.

**Alternatives considered**: *`bytea` columns* (bloats the database and every `SELECT *`); *MinIO/S3 container* (a third compose service, which the feature's two-service constraint rules out); *ABP Settings instead of `IOptions`* (deferred — adopt if an admin UI for limits is ever requested).

---

## 8. Condition and circulation state semantics

**Decision**:
- `ToolCondition` = `New | Good | Worn | Damaged` — the fixed scale from the product spec. **Any** value may follow any other (a repair can improve condition); a transition to the *same* value is rejected as a no-op. Condition cannot change while an instance is `Retired`.
- `ToolInstanceCirculationState` = `InCirculation | Retired`. Registration always starts `InCirculation`. `Retire(reason)` is allowed only from `InCirculation` and requires a non-empty reason (≤ 512 chars). **`Retired` is terminal in this feature** — un-retiring is out of scope.
- **Availability** (the filter in FR-007 and the flag in the public contract) = `CirculationState == InCirculation && Condition != Damaged`.

**Rationale**: The product spec presents New→Good→Worn→Damaged as a *scale*, not a one-way ratchet; forcing monotonic decay would make the Maintenance feature (003+) unable to record a successful repair without a workaround. Excluding `Damaged` from availability gives the availability filter real meaning in a slice that has no loans yet, and it is the semantics Lending will keep — Lending narrows availability further (`… && not currently on loan`) without changing this contract.

**Alternatives considered**: *monotonic condition transitions* (blocks Maintenance); *availability = `InCirculation` only* (makes the filter a duplicate of the retired filter and would need a breaking contract change once Maintenance lands).

---

## 9. Append-only history representation

**Decision**: One child entity `ToolInstanceStateChange` inside the `ToolInstance` aggregate records **every** transition — registration, condition change and retirement — as a single row capturing both dimensions: `PreviousCondition?`, `NewCondition`, `PreviousCirculationState?`, `NewCirculationState`, `Reason`, `ChangedAt`, `ChangedByUserId`. Registration writes the first row with both `Previous*` values `null`. Rows are never updated or deleted; corrections are new rows.

**Rationale**: Principle IV. A single row-per-transition shape means the history is a straightforward chronological ledger — no need to join two parallel history tables to reconstruct "what did this instance look like on date X". Modelling it as a child of the aggregate lets the domain guarantee that no state change can be persisted without its history row, because both happen in one `SaveChanges`.

**Alternatives considered**: *Separate `ConditionChange` and `RetirementRecord` tables* (two append-only stores to keep consistent, and reconstruction needs a merge-sort); *EF Core temporal tables* (not supported by Npgsql, and it would put the audit rule in the database rather than the domain).

---

## 10. Cross-module integration mechanism

**Decision**: Publish `ToolInstanceStateChangedEto` (defined in `ToolShare.Catalog.Application.Contracts`) by calling `AddLocalEvent(...)` on the `ToolInstance` aggregate root; ABP's unit of work dispatches it on `SaveChanges`. Downstream modules subscribe with `ILocalEventHandler<ToolInstanceStateChangedEto>`. Synchronous queries go through `IToolInstanceLookupAppService`.

**Rationale**: `AddLocalEvent` on the aggregate ties event publication to successful persistence — a handler can never observe a state change that was rolled back, which a manual `ILocalEventBus.PublishAsync` inside an application service cannot guarantee. Together the two channels are exactly the coupling Principle II permits, and nothing else is exposed.

**Alternatives considered**: *`IDistributedEventBus`* (correct for a future extraction to services, but adds an outbox and a broker to a monolith that needs neither today — the constitution names `ILocalEventBus`); *direct app-service calls between modules* (explicitly forbidden).

---

## 11. Authorization boundary and seeding

**Decision**: A `Catalog` permission group with `Catalog.Categories`, `Catalog.Tools`, `Catalog.ToolInstances` and their `.Create` / `.Edit` / `.Delete` / `.Retire` / `.ManagePhotos` children (see [contracts/catalog-permissions.md](./contracts/catalog-permissions.md)). Browsing is `[Authorize]` with **no** specific permission, so any authenticated user can read. Seed a `Librarian` role granted the Catalog management permissions; the template's `IdentityDataSeedContributor` already seeds the `admin` user and the `admin` role holds all permissions. The role seeder lives in the **host** `ToolShare.Application` project (which may reference `Catalog.Application.Contracts` for the permission-name constants), so Catalog never takes a dependency on the Identity module.

**Rationale**: FR-011/FR-012/FR-013 and US3's independent test all follow directly. Seeding `Librarian` costs one contributor and makes "a signed-in user *without* Catalog management permission" testable without waiting for the Membership feature — while staying inside the spec's assumption that full member management is deferred. Multi-tenancy stays disabled (`MultiTenancy.IsEnabled = false`); the template's tenant plumbing is left untouched rather than surgically removed.

**Alternatives considered**: *Admin-only, no Librarian role* (leaves FR-012's "restricted to the Librarian/Administrator role" only half-demonstrated); *seeding the role from inside Catalog* (couples a business module to the Identity module); *ripping multi-tenancy out of the template* (a large, risky edit for zero functional gain).

---

## 12. Concurrency conflict detection (FR-010)

**Decision**: Rely on ABP's `IHasConcurrencyStamp`, which every `AggregateRoot<Guid>` already implements. `Update*Dto`s carry `ConcurrencyStamp`; the application service passes it to the repository, and the resulting `AbpDbConcurrencyException` is translated at the Blazor layer into a user-facing "this record was changed by someone else — reload and retry" message.

**Rationale**: Built into the chosen stack, covered by EF Core's optimistic-concurrency machinery against real PostgreSQL (hence testable under the Testcontainers setup), and requires no bespoke versioning column.

**Alternatives considered**: *`xmin` system column as the token* (Npgsql-specific and invisible in the domain model); *last-write-wins* (fails FR-010).

---

## 13. Containerization

**Decision**: One multi-stage `Dockerfile` — `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` restores/publishes **both** `ToolShare.Blazor` and `ToolShare.DbMigrator` into `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0`. `docker-entrypoint.sh` runs `dotnet ToolShare.DbMigrator.dll` when `RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` (compose default), then `exec dotnet ToolShare.Blazor.dll`. `docker-compose.yml` defines `postgres` (`postgres:16-alpine`, named volume, `pg_isready` healthcheck) and `app` (`depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy`, blobs volume).

**Rationale**: Satisfies FR-014/FR-016 and the feature's explicit two-service shape while keeping Principle VI's "migrations by a dedicated DbMigrator, never implicitly at request time" literally true — see the boundary note in [plan.md](./plan.md). Waiting on the health check rather than a sleep gives FR-020 a clear failure mode: the migrator exits non-zero with the Npgsql error instead of the app serving empty pages. **[verified]** Docker 29.6.2 is available on this machine.

**Alternatives considered**: *Separate `dbmigrator` compose service* (a third service, outside the stated scope); *`Migrate()` in the host's startup* (direct Principle VI violation); *two Dockerfiles* (duplicated restore layers and a slower build for no benefit).

---

## Resolved unknowns summary

| Technical Context item | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Platform + how to generate it | .NET 10 / ABP 10.5.0 via repo-local legacy `Volo.Abp.Cli` 10.5.0 — **[verified]** produces `net10.0` and builds. Matches constitution v2.0.0 Principle I (amended from .NET 9). |
| SDK selection | `global.json` pinning `10.0.301`, `rollForward: latestFeature` — **[verified]** installed |
| EF Core design-time tooling | `dotnet-ef` **must be 10.x**; the machine's global 9.0.9 **[verified]** fails migration scaffolding against the .NET 10 runtime |
| xUnit v2 vs v3 on .NET 10 | **[verified]** ABP 10.5 still generates xUnit 2.9.3 — no test-framework migration in scope |
| Blazor interactivity model | InteractiveServer only; WASM/HttpApi.Client projects removed (**[verified]** ABP 10.5 still defaults to InteractiveAuto) |
| Module packaging shape | Six sibling `Catalog.*` projects, not the `-t module` template |
| Per-module migration wiring | Module-owned `ICatalogDbSchemaMigrator`; `DbMigrator` composes |
| Integration-test database | Testcontainers `postgres:16-alpine`, template-database clone per test class; SQLite removed |
| Accent/case-tolerant search | Persisted `NormalizedName` from a pure domain normalizer |
| Photo storage + limits | ABP BlobStoring FileSystem; `CatalogPhotoOptions` (5 MB, jpeg/png/webp, 5 per instance) |
| Condition/circulation rules, availability | Free condition transitions (no no-ops, not while retired); `Retired` terminal; available = in circulation ∧ not damaged |
| History shape | Single append-only `ToolInstanceStateChange` covering both dimensions |
| Cross-module channel | `AddLocalEvent` → `ILocalEventBus`; `IToolInstanceLookupAppService` for queries |
| Permission boundary + bootstrap | `Catalog` group; browse = authenticated; seeded `admin` + `Librarian` role |
| Concurrency | ABP `ConcurrencyStamp` → `AbpDbConcurrencyException` → UI conflict message |
| Container topology | Multi-stage Dockerfile, entrypoint runs DbMigrator then host; two compose services |
